reproduced_defect.name: empty Responses input erases persistent segment context identity
mechanism: response_input_fingerprints() mixes tools/prompt/text context into each input-item fingerprint but emits an empty tuple when input=[]
therefore two empty-input requests with different tools/instructions/prompt context both produce ()
input_prefix_length((), ()) returns 0, so current server segment logic does not classify the context change as history_rewritten

V12 durable_replay_fingerprint detects exact-request identity changes, but it does not by itself force a new Notion segment when the replay fingerprint differs; the segment can still be continued under stale tool/prompt context
reproduced_defect.risk: After restart or on a later request with empty prior history, Core can continue a Notion thread whose planner/tool contract was created under different tools or application context. For a legacy empty segment, an appended first item can also anchor to context of unknown identity because empty history is a prefix of every history.

rules: persist a separate content-free request-context fingerprint per ConversationSegment; do not derive segment context identity only from per-input-item hashes
context fingerprint must cover bridge prompt-policy fingerprint, engineer instructions when applicable, tools, tool_choice and text response contract; model remains covered separately
if a persisted context fingerprint exists and differs, roll over to a fresh Notion segment before provider continuation

if a legacy segment lacks context fingerprint and has zero input fingerprints, do not continue it as an anchor: exact empty legacy retry remains fail-closed under V12 legacy logic; a genuinely appended request rolls over with context_identity_unknown
store the context fingerprint in the same strict durable publication as replay/progress so restart cannot lose it
